images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of Reframe: visual agents should produce reliable intermediate results and truly look at them.(a) Outcome-based RL without explicit grounding rewards can permit observation neglect. (b) Vanilla MOPD may supervise trajectories conditioned on a poorly grounded observation state. (c) Our GD-GRPO rewards grounded actions and encourages reliance on tool-returned observations. (d) Our OG-MOPD repairs deficient tool actions before continuing distillation.

Figure 2:Construction pipeline of Reframe-100K.We first collect public data sources and preprocess them into a raw data pool. We then drop samples answerable from text alone, and audit the rest with 8 rollouts on the full input (FF) and on the annotated evidence alone (EE), discarding samples that are (1) too easy or too hard; (2) insufficiently supported by their evidence. Remaining suspicious samples are diagnosed by Qwen and removed only when a final reviewer confirms an answer or evidence error.

Figure 3:Overview of GD-GRPO.The policy samples multi-turn tool-use rollouts. After the first successful tool call, the original inputo0o_{0}is dropped with probability 0.5 while tool-returned observationsoto_{t}remain visible, so the answer must rely on what the tools have retrieved. Rollouts are grouped by their pre-sampled drop flagdid_{i}, and advantages are normalized within each subgroup so that dropout does not confound the comparison.

Figure 4:Overview of OG-MOPD.Tool actions of the student policy are checked against annotated evidence using an IoU threshold. Missing, invalid, or poorly grounded actions are replaced with annotation-derived actions to obtain query-relevant observations. Injected action tokens receive NLL supervision, while retained student-generated tokens are trained with MOPD.
